findings.title: Scroll indicator bridge uses a stateless coordinator wrapper
findings.evidence: HiddenScrollIndicators.swift lines 10-36 keep NSViewRepresentable.makeCoordinator/Coordinator even though Coordinator now only forwards enclosingScrollView lookup and static NSScrollView mutation. The true ownership is the probe view itself.
findings.resolution: HiddenScrollIndicators.swift no longer defines makeCoordinator or a Coordinator type. The bridge is now a direct NSViewRepresentable that owns HiddenScrollIndicatorProbeView, and the probe view itself owns scroll-view discovery and mutation.
findings.verify_evidence: Verified in Sources/NetScopeMenuBar/HiddenScrollIndicators.swift lines 10-133: HiddenScrollIndicatorConfigurator only implements makeNSView/updateNSView, and HiddenScrollIndicatorProbeView owns the fallback lifecycle and NSScrollView configuration.

findings.title: MenuBarModel swallows baseline-store initialization failure
findings.evidence: Sources/NetScopeMenuBar/MenuBarModel.swift currently defaults baselineStore via makeDefaultBaselineStore(), which catches LocalTrafficBaselineStore init failure and returns nil. The model then initializes without any baselineWarning, so learned-baseline persistence can be disabled silently.
findings.resolution: MenuBarModel now resolves the default baseline store inside the initializer, surfaces creation failure as baselineWarning, and tests cover the failing factory path.

findings.title: MenuBarModel saves learned baseline synchronously on the main actor
findings.evidence: Sources/NetScopeMenuBar/MenuBarModel.swift saveBaselineIfNeeded() calls baselineStore?.save(...) directly from the MainActor model after each rolling sample. That mixes disk I/O into the UI and state layer and can stall the menu bar path despite the hard responsiveness constraint in README.
findings.resolution: Baseline save and clear operations now run through BaselinePersistenceController on a utility queue, so MenuBarModel no longer performs baseline file I/O on the MainActor hot path.

findings.title: Popover open enters a 10-second rolling sample loop
findings.evidence: Oracle review plus local inspection confirm AppDelegate.showPopover() marks foreground observation active and RollingObservationScheduler then uses PowerBudget.foregroundObservationSampleSeconds = 10 while the popover remains open, despite README saying rolling samples run no more often than once per minute and high-frequency passive monitoring is out of scope.
findings.resolution: Opening the popover now runs a single interactive observation via AppDelegate.showPopover() and MenuBarModel.observeCurrentActivity(); RollingObservationScheduler no longer has a foreground 10-second loop.
findings.verify_evidence: Direct code inspection plus full swift test pass after the current review fixes.

findings.title: Baseline store load trusts persisted caps and reads unbounded file contents
findings.evidence: LocalTrafficBaselineStore.load() reads the full baseline file into memory and decodes maximumAgeSeconds / maximumApps from disk into TrafficBaseline before prune(). A tampered or corrupted file can bypass runtime caps and grow startup memory beyond the README limits.
findings.resolution: LocalTrafficBaselineStore.load() now caps baseline file reads at PowerBudget.maximumBaselineFileBytes and TrafficBaseline clamps persisted caps during decode before prune().
findings.verify_evidence: TrafficBaselineTests cover oversized baseline rejection and persisted-cap clamping; full swift test passed.

findings.title: Refresh can overlap an in-flight rolling sample
findings.evidence: MenuBarModel.refresh() only guards isLoading, while recordRollingAppCounterSample() also guards isRollingSampleInFlight. A user-triggered path check can therefore overlap a rolling nettop sample, increasing command pressure and reusing stale app evidence.
findings.resolution: MenuBarModel.checkNetworkPath() queues behind interactiveObservation and rollingSample instead of overlapping them, and queued path checks reuse the finished app observation.

findings.title: CommandRunning lets fakes ignore timeout enforcement
findings.evidence: CommandRunning currently provides a default run(_:arguments:timeoutSeconds:) implementation that discards timeoutSeconds and calls the untimed method. Any test double or future adapter can therefore bypass the bounded-command contract unless it remembers to override the timed overload.
findings.resolution: CommandRunning now has a timed requirement and ProcessCommandRunner enforces timeout handling for all implementations, including fakes used in tests.
findings.verify_evidence: CommandRunnerTests exercise default timeout forwarding and timeout enforcement; full swift test passed.

findings.title: Popover open path does not collect the Wi-Fi metrics promised by README interactive observations
findings.evidence: README says opening the popover starts interactive observations that sample per-app counters and read Wi-Fi link state. The code path currently uses recordRollingAppCounterSample(), which calls captureRollingAppCounters() and leaves wifi nil.
findings.resolution: SnapshotService.captureInteractiveObservation() includes Wi-Fi probing with privacyMode .linkMetricsOnly, so popover-open observations now collect the README-promised passive Wi-Fi metrics without ping.
findings.verify_evidence: SnapshotServiceTests.interactiveObservationsDoNotRunPingProbe asserts wifi is present; full swift test passed.
